name: unity-driver
summary: Run the Unity editor unattended from the shell: compile check, run an editor method, run EditMode and PlayMode tests, at a chosen profile (blind, agent, human), with a machine-wide cap on engines and dedicated environments for parallel work.
adapt: Add Logs/ to .gitignore if it is not there already (Unity's own template ignores it).
Let Unity create Gam3Profile.cs.meta (the next compile does it) and commit it with the script.
For `test`: the project needs com.unity.test-framework in Packages/manifest.json and at least one test assembly.
Use --profile blind for compile and for tests that do not read pixels; keep --profile human for the final look.

verified.how: In a small built-in-pipeline project. 0.1.0 checks (compile ok and failed, exec arguments, exceptions, exit codes, missing method, EditMode tests, refusal while another editor holds the project) still hold. New in 0.2.0: compile, EditMode and PlayMode test runs under blind (-nographics), agent and human; under blind and agent a play-mode test measured 300 frames = 10.000 s of game time (fixed 1/30 s step), under human real time; the quality level dropped to the lowest under agent and ProjectSettings/QualitySettings.asset was byte-identical afterwards; a capture under blind was refused; --stay with a method that never exits was stopped by --timeout; a second run on the same project was refused while the first ran; two editors ran side by side on two environments made by env.mjs (Library cloned); with GAM3_MAX_ENGINES=1 the second run waited for the slot and then ran. Seconds and peak memory in KIT.md are from these runs. Two of about sixty runs took 79 s and 468 s instead of about 5 s while other engines were starting; they passed and the cause was not found. Not run: Windows, Linux, URP, HDRP, more than two editors at once.
